note: Claude Code feature → detectable signal → finding it addresses. Same entry shape as catalog.json; /orangu:improve may refresh from the changelog online, adding candidates with verifiedAt null. All URLs from the public docs

entries.note: An output style is part of the system prompt (cached in the prefix, survives compaction, per the public docs). A style that limits verbosity addresses repeated output bursts of 8k tokens or more. Output tokens are the ones that the model generates one at a time.

context: fork (+ agent, background) runs a skill in a subagent instead of the main thread. Fork subagents inherit the conversation and reuse the prompt cache, so a heavy skill no longer inflates the main context. This addresses a skill whose token weight per invocation is a multiple of the median turn.

Skills, agents, and --effort accept an effort level. Set it low for mechanical steps that spend thinking tokens on single-tool requests. An effort change keeps the prompt cache by default on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and on Fable 5.1 from Claude Code 2.1.260. This holds with an API key or a Claude subscription. On most other models, each effort level has its own cache, so keep one level for each agent or skill during a session.

Long-running commands can run detached (Bash run_in_background) and agents can carry background frontmatter, so a slow tool stops blocking the turn. This addresses tools with p95 over 30 s that the session waits on serially.

As a declared workflow, an agent tree 3 levels deep is leaner to run and easier to reason about. The wf_ runs are first-class, and the artifacts of each run are stored under the session directory. Use a declared workflow instead of ad-hoc nested spawns.

A procedure that you type again in every session belongs in a skill. Its description gates loading, so the skill stays out of context until needed. Bundled scripts run without entering context at all. Invoked bodies survive compaction (capped at 5k tokens each, per the public docs).

A PostToolUse hook can run the test or build gate of the project automatically after edits. Hooks run as code, not as context. This addresses sessions that end with edited files and no test or build run.

Run /usage in Claude Code before you change a subagent. On a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise plan, it breaks your usage down by skill, subagent, plugin and MCP server. So it shows the share of your usage that each subagent type takes. This built-in command is the first check, before a proposal.

Run /usage in Claude Code to see the Prompt cache (main) line of the session. It shows the hit ratio, the miss count and whether the cache is warm now. When Claude Code can find one, the line also names the likely cause of the last miss. The line needs Claude Code 2.1.251 or later, and the likely cause needs 2.1.260 or later. The line covers the main conversation, and this finding also counts subagent requests, so the two ratios can differ.

Run /doctor in Claude Code for a setup checkup. Its extension check compares unused skills, MCP servers and plugins with the context that they take, and it finds slow hooks. Claude reports its findings first and changes nothing before you confirm.

Run /skill-doctor in Claude Code to see how much context each skill takes and how often it runs. It flags the skills in the listing that never ran, and it says where to turn them off. It needs Claude Code 2.1.252 or later and feature-flag fetching. This finding counts the tokens of each run of a skill, which is a different measure.

If many of the waits are permission prompts in Manual mode, run /fewer-permission-prompts in Claude Code. It scans your recent transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP calls, and it adds them to an allowlist in .claude/settings.json. New terminal sessions start in auto mode, where a classifier reviews a risky command before it runs.

Run /context in Claude Code to see the context use of the session as a colored grid. It suggests changes for context-heavy tools and memory bloat, and it gives capacity warnings. Use it to find the largest part of the baseline before you trim CLAUDE.md or remove an MCP server.
